subject: nvidia
top3: NVIDIA가 OCP Global Summit에서 **Vera Rubin 랙 설계**를 공개 기증해 데이터센터 업계 표준화를 주도한다.
LTTS와 NVIDIA가 벵갈루루에 **AI 네이티브 제조 랩**을 공동 개설해 스마트 팩토리 혁신을 가속화한다.
NVIDIA가 사상 최대인 **1,500억 달러 자사주 매입** 계획을 공시해 주주환원 의지를 강조했다.

action.action: Vera Rubin 랙 및 컴퓨트 트레이 설계를 OCP(Open Compute Project)에 MGX 아키텍처를 통해 기여하고, DSX AI Factory용 오픈소스 소프트웨어 컴포넌트 및 다수 파트너십(네트워킹 표준, 전력 설계 등)을 발표

action.scope: NVIDIA Vera Rubin 기반 AI 팩토리 전체(랙, 네트워킹, 전력, 냉각, 소프트웨어), 하이퍼스케일러 및 OEM/파트너 생태계 대상

key_facts: NVIDIA가 **Vera Rubin 랙·컴퓨트 트레이 설계를 MGX 아키텍처를 통해 OCP에 기여**
MGX 1.2 규격은 랙당 최대 250kW 배치를 지원하며 5,000A 버스바, 블라인드메이트 액체냉각, 19인치 장비 지원 추가
Vera CPU 랙 설계는 tool calling, orchestration, sandboxed execution 등 에이전틱 AI를 위한 전용 플랫폼으로 MGX 3세대 아키텍처 기반
NVIDIA와 Cisco가 400Gb/s 기반 네트워킹 패브릭용 업계 최초 USFP(Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable) 표준 발표
NVIDIA와 Google이 미래 ConnectX-10 SuperNIC 및 BlueField DPU에서 Falcon Transport 지원 발표
Meta와 NVIDIA가 Spectrum-X Ethernet SuperNIC 및 Spectrum-6 기반 개방형 AI 네트워킹 발전 발표
summary_data.why_matters: AI 인프라가 메가와트에서 기가와트 규모로 확장되는 가운데, **NVIDIA가 핵심 랙·전력·냉각 설계를 개방형 표준(OCP/MGX)으로 제공**함으로써 하이퍼스케일러·OEM들이 더 빠르고 상호운용 가능한 방식으로 Vera Rubin 기반 AI 팩토리를 구축할 수 있게 한다. 이는 Cisco, Google, Meta 등 주요 플레이어들과의 네트워킹·전력 표준 협력을 통해 NVIDIA 아키텍처를 업계 표준으로 고착시키는 전략으로 해석된다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 Vera Rubin 세대 하드웨어 설계를 **개방형 표준으로 선제 공개**함으로써 생태계 전체(부품 제조사, 하이퍼스케일러, OEM)를 자사 아키텍처에 맞춰 조율하고, 이를 통해 tokens-per-watt 성능과 배포 속도에서 경쟁 우위를 유지하려는 전략을 보여준다.

related.title: OCP Global Summit: Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide
Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide

cards.body: As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more reliably. At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at creating a common foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure. NVIDIA contributed key NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs to OCP through the open NVIDIA MGX architecture, giving system builders a common foundation for developing next-generation AI factory infrastructure. Together, these efforts span the AI factory itself, the utility grid that powers it and the rack-scale architecture at the heart of modern accelerated computing. NVIDIA and Partners Announce Open Architecture Advances At the OCP event, NVIDIA and partners made a handful of announcements: NVIDIA and hyperscalers published open standards for next-generation AI factories, including AI factory design standards and grid resilience. NVIDIA launched new open source software components for NVIDIA DSX AI Factory. Meta and NVIDIA advanced open AI networking with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet SuperNIC and Spectrum-6 innovations. Visionbay introduced an 800V DC AI factory design for the Vera Rubin era. NVIDIA and Cisco announced the Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP) standard, the industry’s first module ​for 400Gb/s-based networking fabrics. NVIDIA and Google announced Falcon Transport support on future NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNICs and BlueField DPUs. Before a packed audience, Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA, discussed how open infrastructure is becoming a critical ingredient for scaling AI factories worldwide. The news at OCP spotlights how NVIDIA’s extreme codesign combined with open standards is accelerating deployment, improving power efficiency and driving tokens-per-watt performance. Vera Rubin AI Factories Advance With MGX Rack Contributions at OCP NVIDIA joined industry leaders in contributing to the third-generation MGX AI data center reference design through OCP’s Open DC Initiative. Combined with open liquid-cooling technologies such as MQD and MQDB, the effort helps turn proven AI factory designs into industry standards that others can adopt, manufacture and scale. For NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories, the updated MGX 1.2 specification extends the open architecture for AI factories with rack-scale blind-mate liquid cooling, interoperable rack-scale interconnect infrastructure and a liquid-cooled 5,000A busbar designed for higher-power AI systems. It also adds native 19-inch equipment support and higher-density rack designs. summary_data.korean_summary: NVIDIA가 미국 고등교육 연구기관의 의학·에너지·소재 분야 혁신을 가속화하기 위해 향후 5년간 10억달러 규모의 초지능 인프라 구축에 투자하기로 했다.

action.action: 미국 내 고등교육 연구기관 지원 등 초지능(슈퍼인텔리전스) 역량 구축에 투자
action.scope: 미국 내 고등교육 연구기관, 의학·에너지·소재 분야

key_facts: NVIDIA는 **향후 5년간 총 10억달러(약 1조3300억원)** 투자를 2026년 10월 12일 공식 발표했다
Jensen Huang CEO가 10월 8일(현지시간) 워싱턴 DC '사이언스: 뉴 골든 에이지' 행사에서 투자 계획을 밝혔다
투자 목적은 미국 과학자들에게 고도화한 초지능을 제공해 **의학, 에너지, 소재 분야 혁신**을 가속화하는 것
Huang은 '미국은 과학 주도권을 산업 주도권으로 전환하고 혁신을 일자리와 기회로 바꿀 것'이라고 발언
투자금은 미국 내 고등교육 연구기관 지원, 양자컴퓨팅 관련 분야 등에 배분될 예정(세부 배분 내용은 본문에서 미확인)
summary_data.why_matters: 이번 투자는 NVIDIA가 단순 하드웨어 공급자에서 **국가 과학 인프라 조성자**로 영향력을 확장하는 행보로, 미국 정부·학계와의 전략적 결속을 강화한다. 경쟁사들이 AI 칩 성능 경쟁에 집중하는 사이 NVIDIA는 연구 생태계 전반을 선점해 장기적 수요 기반을 다지려는 것으로 해석된다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 GPU·AI 플랫폼 판매를 넘어 **미국 과학 연구 인프라에 직접 투자**함으로써 자사 기술을 국가 혁신 전략의 핵심 축으로 위치시키고 있다.

summary_data.korean_summary: NVIDIA와 Cisco가 레인당 400Gb/s 전기 신호를 지원하는 첫 모듈인 USFP(Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable)를 공동 발표해, AI 팩토리가 네트워크 계층 추가 없이 더 많은 컴퓨팅 시스템을 연결할 수 있도록 Ethernet AI 패브릭 확장을 지원한다.

action.action: 레인당 400Gb/s를 지원하는 고밀도 광모듈 규격 USFP 공동 발표 및 TE Connectivity, Amphenol과 하드웨어 생태계 구축
action.scope: 스위치 및 SuperNIC용 OSFP 사이즈 트랜시버, 16레인(향후 32레인 이상 확장 가능)

key_facts: USFP는 **레인당 400Gb/s 전기 신호를 지원하는 최초의 모듈**로 설계되었으며 전체 용량 최대 12.8Tb/s 달성 가능
200Gb/s-per-lane 광모듈 대비 **4배의 대역폭 밀도와 약 1.3배의 전력 효율** 제공
첫 USFP 기반 트랜시버는 OSFP 사이즈 폼팩터에 16개 풀듀플렉스 레인을 탑재, 향후 32레인 이상으로 확장 가능
별도의 전용 임베디드 냉각 회로 없이 최대 100W 전력 소모 지원
NVIDIA, Cisco는 TE Connectivity, Amphenol과 함께 USFP 기반 멀티소스 하드웨어 생태계 구축 중
summary_data.why_matters: AI 모델과 추론 수요 확대로 AI 팩토리는 네트워크 복잡성, 전력, 비용을 관리하면서 더 많은 컴퓨팅 시스템을 연결해야 하는데, **USFP는 네트워크 계층 추가 없이 1.6Tb/s 엔드포인트를 더 많이 연결**할 수 있게 해 이러한 확장 과제를 해결한다. 이는 광학 인터커넥트 분야에서 NVIDIA가 네트워킹 파트너(Cisco)와 커넥터 업체(TE Connectivity, Amphenol)를 아우르는 생태계를 주도하려는 움직임으로, 차세대 AI 네트워크 표준을 선점하려는 경쟁 구도를 보여준다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 GPU·네트워킹을 넘어 **광학 인터커넥트 폼팩터 표준화까지 생태계를 확장**함으로써 AI 팩토리 전체 스택(실리콘-시스템-옵틱스-네트워크 OS)에서의 지배력을 강화하려는 전략을 보여준다.

cards.body: News Summary: - Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP) is designed to be the first module to support 400Gb/s-per-lane electrical signals, enabling capacity up to 12.8Tb/s so AI factory builders can scale Ethernet AI fabrics, while extending a proven deployment model across multiple generations of data center networks. - USFP delivers 4x the bandwidth density and 1.3x the power efficiency of 200Gb/s-per-lane optics so AI factories can connect more computing systems without adding network tiers, while using less power to move each bit of data. - NVIDIA and Cisco are working with TE Connectivity and Amphenol to build a multi-source hardware ecosystem around USFP. NVIDIA and Cisco today announced plans for Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a new high-density 400Gb/s-per-lane optical module designed to equip the hardware ecosystem for the next generation of AI factories using pluggable transceivers. As AI models grow and inference demand expands, AI factories must connect more computing systems while managing network complexity, power and costs. Moving more data per watt and per switch helps operators make better use of their infrastructure investments. Scaling AI factories requires more bandwidth per connection and more connections per switch. When a switch reaches its capacity, further network expansion can require additional switch layers and optical links, increasing latency, power consumption and costs. USFP is designed to enable AI factory builders to scale from 200 Gb/s per lane to 400Gb/s-per-lane Ethernet AI fabrics, while extending a deployment model proven at scale across multiple generations of data center networks. With USFP, customers can embrace next-generation optical technology and meet the performance demand of AI workloads without overhauling their data center infrastructure. The first planned USFP-based transceivers will pack 16 full-duplex lanes in an octal small form factor (OSFP)-sized footprint supporting both switches and SuperNICs, with the ability to expand to 32 and more lanes in the future. By doubling both the lane count and bandwidth per lane, USFP enables AI fabrics to connect more 1.6Tb/s endpoints without adding network tiers. Customers will be able to achieve 12.8Tb/s of overall capacity with USFP. Comparable with an OSFP-sized module, it delivers 4x the bandwidth and front-panel bandwidth density, with approximately 1.3x the power efficiency, versus 200Gb/s-per-lane pluggable modules. This means AI builders can increase their compute scale within the same network footprint, while decreasing networking’s share of the overall AI factory power budget. “Building the world’s largest AI factories starts with rethinking the smallest of connections,” said Gilad Shainer, senior vice president NVIDIA. “With USFP, NVIDIA and Cisco are building an ecosystem to reinvent pluggable optics — connecting more computing with greater efficiency to power the next generation of AI factories.” “AI builders need an in

cards.body: Seven months after his initial arrest for allegedly conspiring to smuggle Nvidia AI chips into China, Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun has pled guilty to four counts. Sun entered the pleas in a Manhattan federal court on October 9. The charges he’s admitted to include conspiracies to violate export controls, smuggle goods, defraud the US, and obstruct justice. His sentencing date has been scheduled for September 8, 2027. Sun was one of three Supermicro workers whom the US government charged with illegally smuggling Nvidia GPU servers into China. The indictment claims that some $2.5 billion in servers were shipped to China, despite Supermicro lacking a Commerce Department license. The accused included Supermicro’s co-founder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, who resigned from Supermicro’s board of directors following his arrest. In early April, he pled not guilty to the charges in a Manhattan federal court. At the time of the arrests, prosecutors allege that the scheme involved the defendants repackaging Supermicro servers into unmarked boxes to disguise the contents and using ‘dummy’ replica servers to fool audits. Surveillance footage shows individuals using a hair dryer to move serial numbers from real servers to dummy servers. The defendants then used a company based in Southeast Asia as a “pass-through entity” to ship the chips from Taiwan to China using third parties. According to the indictment, the pass-through entity became one of Supermicro’s largest customers in 2024, accounting for $99.7 million in revenue in the final quarter of that financial year. No charges have been brought against Supermicro, and earlier this year, the company publicly declared it was “committed to protecting our advanced technologies and intellectual property,” revealing in a statement that it had been working “closely with the Taiwanese authorities” to prevent the "illicit diversion of our highly sought-after systems into the restricted China market.“ As a result of the collaboration, the authorities have seized 50 servers that had been “deceptively acquired after being sold by Supermicro to an authorized reseller,” the company said at the time. Following reports that its Taiwanese office was raided in June 2026, the company published an open letter stating that the authorities had confirmed that Supermicro “is not the target of this investigation,” adding that its offices in Taiwan were not in fact raided by any government authorities, as was “widely misreported.” However, the company did confirm that four of its employees in Taiwan had been detained for questioning with regard to the company’s sale of products to an unnamed technology firm in the country, and that Supermicro had cooperated with authorities to provide access to the desks and electronic devices of those workers. Two of the four employees have been detained pending a hearing, while the other two have been released on bail.

related.title: Nvidia gears up to smash CPU hegemony as Vera starts shipping

cards.body: Nvidia’s Vera CPU offerings have commenced shipping in “multiple form factors,” the company confirmed. Speaking ahead of the OCP Global Summit in San Jose, Joe DeLaere, Nvidia’s product lead for AI infrastructure solutions, said in a press briefing that dedicated Vera racks were “shipping now.” The Vera CPU rack platform leans on Nvidia’s MGX modular reference architecture and acts as a dedicated side-cabinet for handling agentic workloads. The “discrete system” placed next to an NVL72, as DeLaere described it, is separated from the core Vera Rubin platform, as the CPUs in an NVL72 are “dealing with other types of orchestration management,” leaving not enough cores to perform tasks needed in agentic workflows. DeLaere told press that Vera provides more than two-fold performance on agentic workloads compared to the previous Grace generation, measured using the SPEC CPU 2026 benchmark. He also cited 1.8-fold performance on Terminal Bench, which he described as measuring agent tasks involving real code running in real containers. “If you get a Vera CPU rack, it's got over 20,000 cores available for agents to operate quickly and complete these tasks as fast as possible,” DeLaere explained during a briefing. “Because Vera CPU was designed specifically for agents with its high bandwidth and its high single-threaded performance, we see that it really accelerates the agentic tool calling and execution of code … and having those separate is really how we can achieve these tremendous agentic workload benchmarks.” Nvidia has been gearing up to take on the CPU hegemony of AMD and Intel at a time when the demand for agentic workloads has shaken up the processor space, with Arm even breaking its long-standing licensing wheelhouse to launch physical chips. Nvidia first announced plans for a standalone CPU business at the turn of the year, with the likes of Meta and CoreWeave among early customers. Amazon Web Services is also in line for Vera, with the hyperscaler billing it as an additional compute option for agentic workloads. Vera entered full production in the spring, with it set to replace Grace as Nvidia’s flagship processor. It also marks somewhat of a departure from Nvidia’s traditional reliance on Arm designs for CPUs in that it features a core design developed largely in-house, though it does still use the Arm v9.2-A architecture. In addition to availability as a standalone processor and a dedicated rack platform, Vera will also provide the CPU portion for the Vera Rubin Superchip, also set to release in the latter half of this year.

FiveNines는 설계 관리, 기술 거버넌스, 컨설턴트 조정, 시공성, 조달 전략을 담당
이 시설은 Nexus AI Factory Platform의 일부로, 재생에너지 기반 **180MW 규모의 첨단 인프라 허브** 구축을 목표로 함
Nexus는 이전에 한국 Naver와 모로코에서 500MW 프로젝트(초기 40MW 목표)를 추진한다고 알려졌음
Nexus는 랙당 최대 400kW를 액체 냉각으로 지원 가능하다고 주장
summary_data.why_matters: 이는 **NVIDIA의 차세대 Vera Rubin 플랫폼**이 북아프리카 신흥 데이터센터 시장으로 확장되는 사례로, AI 인프라 수요가 전통적 하이퍼스케일 지역을 넘어 지리적으로 다변화되고 있음을 보여준다. 모로코는 현재 데이터센터 footprint가 작은 지역이지만 재생에너지 기반 AI 팩토리 허브로 부상할 가능성을 시사한다.
summary_data.subject_angle: **NVIDIA의 Vera Rubin NVL72**가 신흥 시장(모로코)의 고밀도 AI 인프라 프로젝트에 조기 채택되는 것은 NVIDIA 플랫폼이 글로벌 AI Factory 확산의 표준 레퍼런스 아키텍처로 자리잡고 있음을 보여준다.

cards.body: Design, engineering, and construction company FiveNines Group and Nexus Core Systems are teaming up to establish a 20MW data center on the outskirts of Casablanca, Morocco. The data center will be designed for high-density AI computing and will house Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems. FiveNines will handle the project’s design management, technical governance, consultant coordination, constructability, and procurement strategy. Gerry Curran, CEO of FiveNines Group, said: “We are delighted to partner with Nexus Core Systems in order to construct an advanced data center in North Africa. This project will bring together our international data center expertise with Moroccan architects, engineers, technical advisers, and relevant authorities.” Bastian Remmlinger, head of infrastructure at Nexus Core Systems, added: “We are very pleased with the cooperation and services FiveNines Group has provided so far. Their team has supported us well as we shape the design and delivery approach for the Morocco data center. We look forward to continuing our work together on this ambitious project.” The data center will form part of the Nexus AI Factory Platform, in which Nexus aims to establish a 180MW "advanced infrastructure hub" that runs on renewable energy. Nexus revealed its plans for a 20MW facility in the region in April 2026. Prior to that, Nexus was said to be working with Korea's Naver on a 500MW project in Morocco. That data center was targeting an initial 40MW. On its website, Nexus Core Systems lists plans for a 12-hectare Moroccan site, as well as plans for a 10MW site in Charlotte, North Carolina, and capacity totaling 40MW across Sweden. The company claims to be able to support up to 400kW per rack via liquid cooling. The 20MW data center in Casablanca is not listed. The company’s CEO and cofounder is listed as Christopher Yoshida, who is a managing partner at boutique global advisory and private investment vehicle Pinetree Partners. He was previously CFO at Northern Data. FiveNines is a UK-based construction company, not to be confused with 5Nines, a colocation provider. The company recently delivered a 9.6MW data center to a hyperscale customer in Austria. Morocco has a small data center footprint at present. Casablanca and Rabat are its largest data center markets, with operators including Orange, N+One, and Inwi.

related.title: Nvidia opens up Vera Rubin rack and tray designs to OCP

cards.body: Nvidia is contributing its Vera Rubin rack and tray designs to the Open Compute Project (OCP), a move it claims will foster open standards. Included in the tech giant’s infra gift are cable-and fan-free liquid-cooled compute trays, interoperable rack-scale interconnect infrastructure, and a liquid-cooled 5,000 amp busbar built for higher-power systems. The Vera Rubin update ties to version 1.2 of its modular reference design standard, MGX. Opening up its infrastructure designs is not a new thing for Nvidia; it previously did the same with Blackwell. The standardization move lets manufacturers build around its platform, while keeping its compute hardware directly intertwined and therefore the center of attention. This latest effort doubles down on liquid cooling, featuring connector solutions for inside trays that allow for cold plates to be swapped out more easily without any unwanted spillage. The MGX 1.2 spec also adds native 19-inch equipment support and higher-density rack designs, and supports rack deployments of up to 250 kilowatts. “The bottleneck for AI factory buildouts is how fast we can manufacture and deploy,” Joe DeLaere, Nvidia’s product lead for AI infrastructure solutions, said during a press briefing. “So when the specification is open, the equipment makers and component developers can start fabricating right away and build a supply chain instead of waiting for a singular customer with one proprietary spec. So overall, that accelerates the entire industry. The ecosystem grows, and we grow with them.” A separate spec extends the MGX beyond GPUs to cover the new Vera CPU rack, which Nvidia revealed has started shipping.

README:  # Model Overview ## Description: The NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark model is the DSpark speculative decoding checkpoint for NVIDIA's Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B model family, which is a hybrid LatentMoE language model designed for reasoning, chat, and agentic workflows. For more information, please check [BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16), [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4). The NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-DSpark-NVFP4 model is intended for DSpark speculative decoding deployments tuned for DGX Spark and low-concurrency data centre workflows. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ## License/Terms of Use: **GOVERNING DOWNLOAD TERMS:** Use of this model is governed by the [OpenMDW-1.1 model license](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/). ## Deployment Geography: Global ## Use Case: Developers deploying Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B for reasoning, chat, RAG, and agentic workflows that benefit from lower-latency speculative decoding on DGX Spark and data centre GPUs. This release is intended for DSpark-assisted serving of Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B rather than as a standalone target model checkpoint. ## Release Date: Hugging Face 08/11/2026 via [https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark) ## References - NVIDIA Model
